correctness.rationale: The exact no-reset survival is (a)_k/k!, and the renewal mass is the coefficient of (1−w)^−b, so at age k the stated weight is its product with (b)_{t−k}/(t−k)!. A reset consumes one step, leaving the gate phase z^k and the claimed off-diagonal element. Differentiating the generating function gives the recurrence; after phase centering at z=e^{2iθ}, division by the leading Legendre normalization gives the stated continuant with positive diagonal D in its imaginary part. Hence for θ in (0,π) and a≠b it cannot have a null vector. At z=1 normalization gives P_t(1)=1. For each fixed t, the leading coefficient stays nonzero on the path from γ=0 through γ<1/2, so the no-crossing argument with P_t=z^t at γ=0 gives t interior roots. Reversal of coefficients swaps a and b and reciprocates nonzero roots, proving the exterior half. At equality the recurrence is Legendre's, with t distinct interior real zeros in the cosine variable and a bijective phase parametrization, giving t simple unit-circle roots. This proves the actual finite-time claim; it does not give a degree-uniform distance from the circle. The supplied checker was inspected but not run.

evidence: Positive Meixner–Pollaczek orthogonality on R holds for λ>0 and θ in (0,π), with weight |Γ(λ+iξ)|² exp((2θ−π)ξ) for real ξ. Positive real orthogonality gives only simple real zeros in ξ for every degree. The classical three-term recurrence at λ=1/2 and ξ=i(a−b)/2 is also exactly the frozen phase-centered recurrence. Wald et al. supply the inverse-age reset model but are not the basis of the zero theorem coverage.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Real-rootedness at nonreal ξ rules out a zero at every admissible θ simultaneously for fixed unequal positive shapes. The frozen determinant is a valid special-case proof from the same classical recurrence, not a gap in its hypotheses.

evidence: At |z|=1 and z≠1, take z=e^{2iθ} with 0<θ<π; e^(−itθ)P_t equals the old polynomial at ξ=i(a−b)/2. At z=1 the coefficient sum is (a+b)_t/t!>0. At b=0 the polynomial is a nonzero scalar multiple of z^t, and at positive shapes exact coefficient reversal swaps a and b.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: On a path of constant positive a+b from b=0 to b<a, no root can cross the unit circle and the degree stays fixed. Reversal puts all roots outside if b>a. At equality and sum one the same generating function specializes to Legendre, as in the published node record. Thus the exact asymmetry and balanced classifications follow, without relying on a scaling limit or an additional conjecture.

originality.rationale: The claimed asymmetric zero exclusion is a direct specialization of classical Meixner–Pollaczek real-rootedness. In fact write P_t(z;a,b) for the frozen polynomial and take λ=(a+b)/2, ξ=i(a−b)/2. Substitute w=e^(−iθ)v in its generating function. Then e^(−itθ)P_t(e^(2iθ);a,b) is exactly the Meixner–Pollaczek polynomial of degree t and parameters (λ,θ), evaluated at ξ: its factors are (1−e^(iθ)v)^(−λ+iξ) and (1−e^(−iθ)v)^(−λ−iξ). Eq. (1.7.5) of Koekoek–Swarttouw and DLMF 18.23.7 give that generating function. Positive orthogonality on R for λ>0 and 0<θ<π makes every zero in ξ real, so evaluating at the nonreal ξ for unequal shapes already excludes the entire unit circle apart from z=1, which is positive. The degree-preserving continuity and coefficient reversal in the frozen proof then give the full strict side classification. This deduction uses a theorem covering every degree and in fact applies along each fixed positive sum a+b, not just a+b=1. The balanced Legendre case was already explicitly treated in the published reset finding. Failure rests on a verified prior implication, not on search quality or exact wording in the prior sources.
residual_risks: The audit does not identify the first publication to phrase the classical implication as a beta-binomial disk theorem; the explicit older generating function and orthogonality suffice to establish coverage.
Not all varying-parameter Jacobi references were read, and no priority is inferred from a same-day catalog date. Neither limitation weakens the exhibited exact reduction.

value.rationale: Finite-time coherence nodes are a meaningful physical question, but the frozen contribution supplies no independently substantive result once the old polynomial is identified. Its all-degree exclusion is a nonreal evaluation of a real-rooted orthogonal polynomial, and the passage from exclusion to a side of the circle is the elementary degree-preserving homotopy and reversal. The balanced physical nodes and reset setup were already available. The record supplies no new quantitative stability, clock extension or other surviving theorem, and the alternative continuant proof is the directly specialized classical recurrence. This is useful as an exposition, not a new finding under the scientific-value standard.
